refused at open: the device compiler fails the store-address probe (ARCH-49)

tests.note: The assembler checks declared access, ownership and races for every module set; the program text of the solver measured at the M0 gate is unchanged. A defect of the Intel integrated GPU compiler found by the tests of the next package is documented and gets a self-test at device open.

packages.title: baseline measurement
packages.note: re-measured interleaved at the gate

packages.title: streaming generator
packages.note: merged; CPU-runtime crash traced to 3-component vector arguments of non-inlined helpers and avoided (D-050)

packages.title: initialisation
packages.note: merged; init bit-exact against the check script at time 0 in both wall modes; cell coordinate is a 4-component vector everywhere (D-050)

packages.title: core modules
packages.note: merged and accepted (D-043): rest state exact, 30-step box with walls within 1.2e-7 of the check script on three devices, plot viewed

packages.title: program integration
packages.note: merged; the program now carries the tag, init and view kernels after the fused kernels

packages.title: prototype driver
packages.note: merged and accepted; host work is 2 % of wall time at 128^3; the mass-drift outlier is 32-bit rounding of the density at 1, reproduced bit for bit by a numpy model (D-054)

packages.title: benchmark harness
packages.note: merged; harness reviewed and corrected before any gate figure was taken (D-055)

packages.title: gate: VAL-12 parity
packages.note: passed: throughput 1.016 (32-bit) and 1.005 (16-bit storage) times the baseline at 256^3, required 0.95; memory 93 and 55 bytes per cell; host work 0.6 % of wall time

packages.title: access and race checks
packages.note: the assembler now rejects module sets whose declared reads and writes do not match their code, two writers of one field, and read-after-write races; two review rounds closed five ways a hidden write could pass

packages.title: scheduler: graph and exchange placement
packages.note: the scheduler now derives, from the declared reads and writes of every pass, where halo exchanges go and which step variants exist; review found and closed two ordering defects, and the rule for two writers of one field is now stated per phase

packages.title: scheduler: consumers and validity
packages.note: diagnostics now register as consumers with their sampling steps, so the output fields are written only on the steps that need them and can be brought up to date on demand; reads inside a callback refer to the sample time; the declared access of generated code is narrowed to what the configuration really writes. Three review passes; a dangling record found by the reviewer was shown by a test and fixed

packages.title: scheduler: finalisation and describe
packages.note: setup now runs as a scheduled sequence that ends with a pass forming the output fields of time 0; the simulation can describe itself as text; parameters can be constants, arrays or time tables, with run-time values checked like configured ones. Two review passes: unchecked run-time values and stale output fields after a changed constant were found, tested and fixed

packages.title: lattice tables and modules
packages.note: five more velocity sets (two- and three-dimensional) with their device modules; tables and moment identities recomputed independently in review

packages.title: compiler self-tests at device open
packages.note: every device is tested when it is opened: a small program with a known exact result is compiled and run, and a device whose compiler gets it wrong is refused with a message that names the test; the Intel UHD 770 with its present driver is refused, the RTX 5050 and the Intel CPU runtime pass

packages.title: streaming on every lattice
packages.note: the streaming generator now serves every lattice (D2Q9, D3Q15, D3Q19, D3Q27 and the scalar sets D2Q5, D3Q7): slot tables, wall tags, initialisation and the views are compared exactly with an independent numpy oracle on the Intel CPU runtime and the RTX 5050, including two negative controls that must fail

packages.title: f16c accessor
packages.note: the second 16-bit storage format (f16c) is available: one integer-only codec shared by host and device, checked against the specification on every 32-bit pattern by the reviewer and against its 31 published vectors on both devices; two injected faults prove that a broken codec stops the run

packages.title: two-array check variant: generator
packages.note: the check variant of the streaming step exists: two copies of the populations with explicit bounce-back, built from the same collision fragments as production; its slot rules match the frozen oracles on six lattices in both wall modes, and the negative control without the second generation differs in exactly the expected elements

packages.title: production equals the check variant bit for bit
packages.note: the production streaming step and the two-array check variant give the same bits: every element of the populations at steps 0, 1, 2, 3 and 100 and the output fields at both parities, on four lattices, in both wall modes, with the SRT, TRT and MRT operators and the three storage types; leaving out the second generation at initialisation changes exactly the predicted number of elements

packages.title: force field, forcing
packages.note: body force per cell: a static force field next to the uniform force / the forcing term in every collision operator / and the preparation pass that makes the state at time 0 consistent with the force (the half-force shift of the velocity). Kolmogorov flow driven by the field recovers the steady sine profile within 0.5 % of its amplitude on D2Q9 (SRT / TRT / MRT) and D3Q19. The review found a wrong number format in one message and gaps around a repeated setup; a repeated setup that would shift the velocity twice now warns and the flag survives a restore

packages.title: sparse fields, host step of finalisation
packages.note: sparse fields: a field that holds a payload only for a listed subset of cells, found on the device through an exact hash table; a host step at setup evaluates the neighbour rules of cell-type groups, builds lists and tables and fills the initial payloads; a first warning channel on the driver. Programs without sparse fields keep their text byte for byte. The review ran three rounds: it closed ways for a fragment to write outside its own cell (one of them older than this package), a silent skip of the host step, an entry limit with 32-bit indices, and halved the time of the host step

packages.title: fragment support for boundary modules
packages.note: fragments of boundary modules can now read their lattice neighbours through one array, know the dimension, ask whether the cell is next to a wall, and require the one-step wall mode; the field write leaves prescribed cells alone. Programs that use none of this keep their text byte for byte. The review found two ways to get past a check, both closed with tests

packages.title: pressure boundary
packages.note: pressure boundary by anti-bounce-back: a cell next to a pressure cell receives the reflected population with the prescribed density and its own velocity of the previous step (kept in a sparse field). A pressure-driven channel recovers the Poiseuille profile to 6e-5 of its maximum; the pressure gradient is 2.6 % above nominal as the spec predicts. The review found no fault in the code but showed that neither the channel nor the host mirror could see an error in the quadratic velocity term; a uniform-flow test where the rule must return the equilibrium exactly closes that (largest deviation 4.5e-8 / a dropped term gives 1.5e-3). The spec had the direction of the end effect reversed; corrected

packages.title: outgoing view, raw state and restore
packages.note: the outgoing view of the populations and its inverse (writing a state through the incoming view), and restart on one block: the raw state of a driver can be taken and restored and the run continues bit for bit, at both step parities. The review found that setup after a restore read the initial store at the wrong parity; fixed with a test. The new kernels are appended to the program text, every byte before them is unchanged

packages.title: sparse payload in the raw state
packages.note: restart with sparse fields: the raw state carries the payload of checkpointed sparse fields (the outlet state of the pressure boundary) and a restore rebuilds the lists and tables from the stored cell types. A run restored into a fresh driver or into one set up with another geometry continues bit for bit. The review found no fault in the new code but a hole from earlier packages: cell types could be rewritten after setup without the lists being rebuilt; the driver now refuses to step until setup has run again

packages.title: force series
packages.note: force series sampled inside run: a series names a set / bodies / a start / an interval and a flush count; run launches the force kernels of a due sample into a device ring and reads the ring once per flush samples / with no other read of the device in the loop. A sample is bit for bit what forces() returns at the same time. Samples are kept over setup() and a restore and returned in sampling order; a flagged sample is a numerical failure at the flush / a take / setup() and a restore; a series whose bodies no longer validate refuses run until it is removed. No generated kernel text changed

packages.title: warning mechanism, storage self-tests
packages.note: warnings as records: every warning carries its requirement / a subject / the text and the step, appears once per requirement and subject, and under the strict policy stops the call that found it (setup and set_parameter). New: the stability warnings of CORE-29 from the largest initial speed and the relaxation time / the force sum checked again when a parameter is set / a valid range for the Smagorinsky constant declared in its manifest. The storage self-tests of the 16-bit formats run once per device where the model is built and choose the hardware or the software variant. The review found one defect (a restore replaced the records only for models with sparse fields) and four test gaps; all closed, tests first

packages.title: run-time health check
packages.note: run-time health check: a module observe.health adds a kernel that counts on the device the cells with a non-finite or saturated population / a density not above zero / a speed above the limit; run enqueues it every interval steps into a device ring of 64 checks and reads 40 bytes per check without blocking; a failed check stops the run with a numerical error naming the condition / its count and the checked step and leaves the driver usable. A diverging run stops at step 107 (velocity) and 114 (density) in f32 / f16s and f16c on both devices; a valid wave at the stability limit never stops. The review found a failed check that could be lost when a checkpoint is taken right after run / closed tests first

packages.title: L2 target, row tables, test geometries
packages.note: the ground for the property tests: a test target l2 with the tiers l2 (every build) and matrix (gates and nightly) / the row tables (21 covering rows in which every pair of factor levels occurs and 264 matrix rows in which every triple occurs) / the test geometries (channel / pipe / sphere / box faces / random walls) / and one shared copy of the random draws. The tiers hold no device test yet; those come with parts b and c. The review recomputed every count with its own scripts and found no fault in a number or a row

packages.title: conservation and symmetry on device sums
packages.note: conservation and symmetry measured with the exact device sums: mass and momentum drift (VAL-7) and mirror and rotation symmetry (VAL-8) on every lattice and collision operator / a short form on every build and the stated form (4 seeds / 10000 steps) at the gates. All values are identical on the CPU runtime and the RTX 5050 and inside their bounds. The per-step mass balance of SRT and TRT is below 2e-10 of the mass (bound fixed from the device values). The momentum drift of MRT is three orders below SRT and TRT / which points at the float equilibrium as the cause of the 32-bit momentum bias (to confirm in M1-14)

packages.title: row rig and the full matrix
L3 target, Couette and Poiseuille
packages.note: the L3 test target and its first physical cases: an every-build tier and a full tier (GPU only) / a data file of frozen thresholds with provenance per key / Couette flow (02-VAL-C1 and C2) on four lattices and three operators / channel and pipe flow (02-VAL-P2 / P3 / P3R) with the force as a parameter and as a field. Every value on the RTX 5050 is inside its spec threshold: Couette 6.8e-6 against 6.8e-5 / channel TRT 2.88e-4 against 2.9e-3 / pipes with margins 1.30 to 1.54. The two MRT channel rows are inside the threshold with small margins (1.20 and 1.27) and far above the 32-bit emulation / which goes to M1-14. Controls show that each test can fail

packages.title: memory check of the two-array variant
measurements: harness and campaign script
packages.note: the tools of the measurement campaign of M1-14: options of the benchmark harness for lattice / operator / box / schedule / extra modules / geometries with bodies / force series and source variants (text transforms of a program with a strict count of replacements); the program olbx_m114 with the call-level measurements and a bit-identity guard of a variant against production (incoming view / raw state / the moments and the writing kernel / forces and a series sample); a quiet-machine verdict (decisions D-084 and D-087) that only observes; transfer counters checked against design values in every record; the tool olbx_kinfo (registers and spills per kernel / device identifiers); a campaign script that runs by section with a dry run / a report generator and seven plots. With no new option the program text / the cache key and the record keys equal M0. The cause of the smoke-test failure IMPL-M1-176 is fixed: a refused busy device is reported as not judged. The campaign itself has not run (part b)

packages.title: momentum bias and MRT channel investigation
packages.note: the cause of the 32-bit momentum bias (open point 10-O4): the binary32 lattice weights give 3 S2 = 1 + 2^-27 on all four lattices / so the collision adds rate x 2^-27 x j per cell and step (rate omega for SRT / omega minus for TRT / 0 for MRT); a host port that is bit-identical to the devices and device tests under label m114 confirm it on the CPU runtime and the RTX 5050. No binary weight table removes it (a proof). The MRT channel levels of 02-VAL-P2 and the Couette imbalance are explained as round-off levels. Stage c3 gives host results only for three projection candidates as a remedy; no device has run a remedy. By decision D-088 the remedy is tested on devices / decided and implemented in package M2-0. Nothing in production changed
